newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO JULY CPI UP 0.87 PERCENT - BANCO DE MEXICO.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO JULY CPI UP 0.87 PERCENT - BANCO DE MEXICO.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 0.87 percent in July from the month before after rising 0.89 percent in June, Banco de Mexico said.
The central bank added that the producer price index rose 0.74 percent in July from the month before.
A survey of 14 Mexican brokerages and research companies found expectations of a rise of 0.88 percent for July's CPI.
The central bank said the decline in July's CPI was the third month in a row inflation was below one percent.
The central bank said that compared with the same month a year earlier the CPI was 19.70 percent higher.
Accumulated inflation rate for the first seven months of the year was 9.61 percent, compared with 16.94 percent in the same period a year earlier.

It said that the main causes of inflation this year was an increase in prices of vegetables and fruits, bus and airplane tickets, hotels, local telephone services, domestic gas, books and other products.
It said that the basic basket of consumer goods rose 0.65 percent in July from the month before.
Banco de Mexico gave the following breakdown for July:
INDEX Percent
Food, drinks and tobacco 0.40
Clothing and shoes 0.44
Housing 0.28
Furniture 0.20
Health and personal care 0.26
Transportation 0.72
Education 0.11
Other services 0.31
The rise of 0.74 percent in July in the producer price index, excluding petroleum, compares to a rise of 1.23 percent in the same month last year.
Compared to July a year earlier the index rose 16.50 percent.
The accumulated increase in the producer price index for the first seven months of this year was 7.85 percent.
((--Robert Kozak, Mexico City newsroom 525 7289559))
